findings: Complete current MDX SHA-256 is ae5cc492ae161e65822b5ae0e300a7a10d777e783ca713ce6436b8734110bae1; all 7 declared sources passed current access review.

Claims remain bounded to adaptable communication practices from university extension sources, professional-representation principles limited to AAPL members, the legal distinction between an informal contact and a power of attorney, and current MRX family-conversation and seller-control boundaries. No source is converted into a private title, probate, authority, consent, value, tax, contract, or transaction conclusion.

The article invents no real owner, property, buyer, contract, transaction, price range, production, reserves, forecast, testimonial, success rate, or owner-specific legal, tax, accounting, title, appraisal, engineering, investment, or transaction conclusion.

sources_inspected.label: University of Minnesota Extension, Preparing to meet with your transition and estate planning team (reviewed 2023; accessed 2026-08-14)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: University of Minnesota Extension transition-planning guidance recommends preparing goals and questions in writing and involving affected people in a fact-based planning process.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article adapts only those preparation practices to defining and routing a narrow family-contact role. It does not treat farm or estate guidance as mineral-rights law or use it to determine ownership, authority, consent, title, value, tax, or whether to sell.

sources_inspected.label: University of Minnesota Extension, Farm business transfer strategies (accessed 2026-08-14)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: University of Minnesota Extension farm-business transfer guidance recommends brief, specific communication that avoids accusation, insult, and blame and describes structured family-business communication.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article adapts only those communication disciplines to neutral acknowledgment and forwarding. It does not equate a mineral interest with a farm business or derive any legal, ownership, authority, consent, valuation, tax, or transaction conclusion from the source.

sources_inspected.label: Utah State University Extension, Estate Planning Toolkit: Starting the Estate Planning Conversation (accessed 2026-08-14)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The Utah State University Extension Estate Planning Toolkit recommends a clear intention, input from people directly affected, an agenda, and recognition that a family discussion may require multiple conversations.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article adapts only those communication practices to establishing and resetting a limited contact protocol. It does not treat the source as mineral-specific advice or use it to determine probate, title, ownership, authority, consent, value, tax, or disposition.

sources_inspected.label: American Association of Professional Landmen, Code of Ethics and Standards of Practice (accessed 2026-08-14)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The American Association of Professional Landmen code addresses fair dealing, accurate representations, confidentiality, competence, and disclosure of interests for AAPL members.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses the source only as a bounded reason to preserve original sender information, written representations, and stated affiliations. It does not imply that every caller is an AAPL member or use the code to validate a person, offer, authority, contract, or transaction.

sources_inspected.label: Texas Law Help, Powers of Attorney Fact Sheet (last legal review 2025-07-31; accessed 2026-08-14)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: Texas Law Help explains that a power of attorney is a legal document that grants another person specified authority and describes distinct kinds and effects of that authority.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses the source only to contrast a non-legal administrative contact protocol with legally operative authority. It does not determine whether a power of attorney exists, is valid, is sufficient, or is appropriate for any reader.

sources_inspected.label: Mineral Rights Xchange, How to Talk to Your Family Before You Decide to Sell Mineral Rights (accessed 2026-08-14)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The current MRX family-conversation guide covers the earlier decision about whether the family wants to receive information or consider later steps.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article links to that guide only as the prerequisite decision boundary. It starts after engagement intent is settled and does not repeat the family-alignment meeting, decide whether to sell, or determine ownership, authority, consent, value, tax, or transaction terms.

sources_inspected.label: Mineral Rights Xchange, Selling Mineral Rights: Selling Process For Mineral Owners (accessed 2026-08-14)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The current MRX seller-control guide separates written proposals, agreements, deeds, payment, delivery, and recording into later transaction states that remain under owner control.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses it only to mark where the point-person protocol ends. It does not retell the selling sequence, compare offers, interpret documents, determine value, negotiate, sign, or recommend a sale.
